title: Data Analysis: Averages, Range & Statistical Interpretation
description: Explore essential mathematical concepts through carefully crafted questions. Strengthen your understanding, practice your reasoning, and learn at your own pace.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the expected value of a set of outcomes with given probabilities.
questions.question: A game has the following outcomes: win \(\$10\) with probability \(0.5\); win \(\$20\) with probability \(0.3\); win \(\$-5\) with probability \(0.2\). What is the expected value of playing this game?
questions.explanation: The expected value is \(E(X) = \sum x \cdot P(x) = (10)(0.5) + (20)(0.3) + (-5)(0.2) = 10\).
questions.hint: Multiply each outcome by its probability, then add the results together.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the range of a data set from its maximum and minimum values.
questions.question: What is the range of the following daily steps (thousands): \(16, 16, 54, 75, 46, 59, 91\)?
questions.explanation: The range is the maximum minus the minimum: \(91 - 16 = 75\).
questions.hint: Subtract the smallest value from the largest value.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish correlation from causation in a real-world statistical claim.
questions.question: A study finds a strong positive correlation between ice cream sales and the number of drowning incidents at beaches during the summer. What is the most statistically sound interpretation?

options.label: A
options.text: Ice cream sales directly cause more drowning incidents

options.label: B
options.text: Drowning incidents directly cause higher ice cream sales

options.label: C
options.text: Both are influenced by a third factor, hot weather, so correlation does not imply causation

questions.explanation: Although the two variables are correlated, this does not mean one causes the other. A lurking variable, warm weather, increases both ice cream sales and the number of people swimming, which in turn increases drowning incidents. This is a classic example of correlation without causation.
questions.hint: Look for a third variable that could independently explain both trends.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret the meaning of a percentile rank in a real-world testing context.
questions.question: A student scored at the \(60\)th percentile on a national test. What does this mean?

options.label: A
options.text: The student answered exactly 60% of the questions correctly

options.label: B
options.text: The student ranked in the top 60% by score, meaning almost everyone scored lower

options.label: C
options.text: The student scored higher than approximately 60% of the students who took the test

questions.explanation: A percentile rank indicates the percentage of scores in the distribution that fall below a given value. Scoring at the \(60\)th percentile means the student performed better than about \(60\%\) of the other test takers, not that they answered \(60\%\) of questions correctly.
questions.hint: A percentile describes relative standing compared to others, not the raw percentage of correct answers.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the mean from data represented in a dot plot.
questions.question: A dot plot shows the number of pets owned by \(6\) students: \(1, 1, 8, 4, 8, 5\). What is the mean number of pets per student?
questions.explanation: Sum the values: \(1 + 1 + 8 + 4 + 8 + 5 = 27\). Divide by the number of students: \(\frac{27}{6} = 4.5\).
questions.hint: Add up all the dots' values and divide by the total number of students.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the range of a data set from its maximum and minimum values.
questions.question: What is the range of the following book pages read: \(40, 33, 13, 56, 66, 12\)?
questions.explanation: The range is the maximum minus the minimum: \(66 - 12 = 54\).
questions.hint: Subtract the smallest value from the largest value.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate whether a described sampling method is likely to introduce bias.
questions.question: A company surveys every 10th customer who exits the store, regardless of who they are, to estimate customer satisfaction. What can be said about this sampling method?

options.label: A
options.text: The sampling method is biased toward frequent shoppers only

options.label: B
options.text: The sampling method is reasonably representative of the population

options.label: C
options.text: The sample cannot be used because it excludes online customers

questions.explanation: In this scenario, this is a reasonably representative systematic sample of the store's customers, which affects whether the results can be generalized to the full population.
questions.hint: Consider whether every member of the population had a fair and equal chance of being included.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate a weighted mean using given weights and values.
questions.question: A student's final grade is weighted as follows: exam 1 (\(40\%\)) score \(89\), exam 2 (\(30\%\)) score \(68\), and project (\(30\%\)) score \(73\). What is the student's weighted average grade?
questions.explanation: Multiply each score by its weight and sum: \(89 \times 0.40 + 68 \times 0.30 + 73 \times 0.30 = 77.9\).
questions.hint: Multiply each score by its weight (as a decimal), then add the results together.

questions.question: A data set of exam scores has no outliers and is roughly symmetric. Which measure of central tendency best summarizes the typical score?
